plainTitle: A taller base for the new affordable housing building at 1337 Queen Street West

sources.label: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning

whatIsProposed.text: City staff recommend that City Council allow the existing building at 1337 Queen Street West to be torn down and a new 16-storey building to be built in its place.

citations.quote: City Council approve the demolition of the non-contributing building and the erection of a new 16-storey mixed-use building at 1337 Queen Street West

whatIsProposed.text: The new building would be a 16-storey tower on a 4-storey base. It would include affordable housing, and the City would keep owning it.

citations.quote: a new 16-storey mixed-use tower with a 4-storey podium building that will include purpose-built affordable housing; and which will remain under ownership of the City

whatIsProposed.text: City Council already approved this project in June 2026. The only change now is that the 4-storey base would be 1.2 metres taller.

citations.quote: A heritage permit for the project was previously approved on June 24 and 25, 2026, by City Council.
All other details of the scheme remain as those approved by City Council in June 2026.

why.text: The base was made taller so the community space on the ground floor can have higher ceilings.

citations.quote: The revised proposal increases the height of the 4-storey podium building by 1.2m in order to increase the floor-to-ceiling heights within the ground floor community space.

why.text: With the taller base, the design no longer follows two rules in the Parkdale Main Street heritage district plan. That is why a new heritage approval is needed.

citations.quote: It also does not include the 5.0m step back required by the PHCD Plan for any parts of the new building that are taller than the adjacent contributing property.
Consequently, a new Section 42 approval under the Ontario Heritage Act is required.

why.text: The building is part of the City-led Parkdale Hub project, which is meant to add affordable rental housing, better community facilities and updated public spaces.

citations.quote: to provide new affordable rental housing, improved community facilities, and modernized public spaces

why.text: Staff's opinion is that the taller base would not harm the heritage character of the area, because this part of Queen Street West does not have a consistent row of building fronts today.
why.caveat: This is the opinion of City staff. No board or Council has agreed or disagreed with it yet.

citations.quote: would not harm the character or appearance of the District or be contrary to the objectives of the PHCD Plan

whoIsAffected.text: The site is on the south side of Queen Street West, between Dunn Avenue and Cowan Avenue, in Ward 4 (Parkdale-High Park).

citations.quote: an interior lot located between Dunn Avenue and Cowan Avenue on the south side of Queen Street West

whoIsAffected.text: Neighbours of the heritage building next door at 1347 Queen Street West: the new base would no longer match that building's height.

citations.quote: it no longer matches the height of the adjacent contributing building at 1347 Queen Street West

whoIsAffected.text: People walking in the area: the design includes a walking route between Dunn Avenue and Masaryk Park.

citations.quote: an east-west pedestrian connection between Dunn Avenue and Masaryk Park

whoIsAffected.text: City budget: staff say this recommendation has no cost to the City budget this year or in future years.

citations.quote: There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Condition: the new building must be built substantially as shown in the architect's plans dated September 25, 2026.

citations.quote: constructed substantially in accordance with the plans and elevations prepared by LGA Architectural Partners dated September 25, 2026

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: A separate minor variance application is also needed for this change.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: The record does not say when that application will be decided or how to comment on it.

citations.quote: A separate minor variance application is also required for the proposed revisions.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Under the heritage district plan, demolition cannot start until City Council has approved the plans for the replacement building and a heritage permit has been issued.

citations.quote: demolition activity shall not begin until plans for the replacement building(s) or structure(s) have been submitted and approved by Toronto City Council, and a heritage permit issued by the City

staff.text: Staff recommend approval, with one condition about following the architect's plans.

citations.quote: It is therefore recommended that City Council approve the application under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

whatHappensNext.text: The Toronto Preservation Board will consider this item on November 16, 2026.

citations.quote: This item will be considered by Toronto Preservation Board on November 16, 2026.

whatHappensNext.text: The staff report is also addressed to Toronto and East York Community Council, and it asks City Council to make the final decision.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The City's item page does not yet list dates for those later steps.

citations.quote: Toronto and East York Community Council
It is therefore recommended that City Council approve the application under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
